# MD-C8 eligibility proposal (A2, candidate)

Study: Johnsen, S., Blenkinsopp, J. and Rayment, M. (2022) Scotland's Housing First Pathfinder evaluation: Final report. Heriot-Watt University. https://doi.org/10.17861/8GJ7-SV28

Proposal: eligible.

Page references give the report pagination first and the PDF page in brackets (roman pages vii-xx = PDF 10-23; arabic page n = PDF n+23).

## Criterion 1: relationship in a public or publicly funded service
- The object is the Housing First Pathfinder in five areas (six local authorities). It provides independent tenancies with open-ended, flexible support from Housing First support workers to people with experience of homelessness and multiple disadvantage (p.vii-ix, PDF 10-12; Chapter 2).
- Funding: Scottish Government £5.8 million (main funder, Years 1-3), Social Bite £2.16 million, Merchants House of Glasgow £150,000 (p.vii, PDF 10; s.1.2, p.3, PDF 26). In the transition year (2021/22) Scottish Government transition funding covered up to half of the cost, and local authorities took over funding after mainstreaming (p.viii, PDF 11; s.7.1.2, p.80-81, PDF 103-104).
- 98% of tenancies are social housing (council or RSL) (s.7.6.1, p.94, PDF 117).
- The relationships studied are those between service users and support workers (s.6.3, "relationality", "stickability", p.62-68, PDF 85-91) and the inter-organisational relationships between support providers, housing providers, health and social care, criminal justice and local authorities (Chapters 7-8).

## Criterion 2: at least one qualitative and one quantitative finding
- Quantitative: Tracker monitoring data for all 579 people housed (tenancy sustainment, Table 5.1, p.49, PDF 72; reasons for ending, Table 5.2, p.51, PDF 74); baseline survey n=80 (s.4.3); staff NDT assessments n=104 (s.4.3.6); follow-up survey n=21 with costed service use (Tables 9.11-9.14, p.141-143, PDF 164-166); financial returns and unit costs (Tables 9.1-9.5).
- Qualitative: interviews and focus groups with 200 participants over three time points, analysed thematically in NVivo (s.1.3, p.4-5, PDF 27-28); non-housing outcomes reported from interviews (s.5.2, p.52-58, PDF 75-81); service user experiences (Chapter 6).

Both criteria are met. Joint claims were not used as a criterion.

## Points for A1
- The service is a mix of public and charitable funding during the Pathfinder; public funding was the main share and the programme became fully publicly funded after mainstreaming. This is read as "publicly funded".
- The evaluation itself was commissioned by Corra Foundation with funding from Social Bite (p.viii, PDF 11).
